title: Tuning rewarded ad frequency in a solo AI-assisted space game
author: Serzhe_Nebulife
selftext:
I’m a solo developer from Ukraine building Nebulife, a space game available on the web, iOS, and Android. I direct the project, and Claude has written almost all of the code and tests. The game uses TypeScript, PixiJS 8 for 2D, Three.js for 3D, React 19, and Capacitor for mobile.

https://reddit.com/link/1xwx4yl/video/55vv39cnfs1i1/player

One of the hardest rules to tune was how often to offer an optional short rewarded ad. If it appeared too rarely, it earned very little for the game; too often, it could become tiring. One player saw three offers in one day and then started skipping them. I settled on one offer per player per day, with rewards adjusted by country. That is one observation, not a broad measurement of player behaviour.



Nebulife’s planets are fully procedural and use no textures. Its shared universe grows from one seed, with player changes persisted by the server, and life evolves according to procedural rules built around a model of natural laws. The attached gameplay clip travels from a galaxy view toward a star system and planet; it does not show evolution, persistence, or the ad flow.



When you have only a small amount of player feedback, how do you decide when a monetization rule is ready to keep or needs another revision?
